source_text:
Fragmenta in epistulam i ad Corinthios
1 Kor 10,15 Ἐν τούτοις ἀπὸ τῆς τῶν παλαιῶν αὐτοὺς παραθέσεως παιδεῦσαι
βούλεται τὰ προσήκοντα, δεικνὺς κἀκείνους καθάπερ ἔν τινι τύπῳ τῶν ἴσων
ἀξιωθέντας· οὕτω γὰρ καταλλήλου φαινομένου τοῦ παραδείγματος εὑρίσκετο
δικαίως αὐτοῖς παραινῶν μὴ τὰ ὅμοια πλημμελεῖν, ἵνα μὴ τὰ ὅμοια πείσωνται. τὸ
μὲν οὖν ὑπὸ τὴν νεφέλην αὐτοὺς εἶναι δήλωσις ἦν τῆς τοῦ πνεύματος χάριτος·
ἐκείνους τε γὰρ ἡ νεφέλη σκιάζουσα τῆς ἐκ τῶν Αἰγυπτίων βλάβης ἀπήλλαττεν, καὶ
ἡμᾶς ἡ χάρις τῆς δαιμονικῆς ἐξαιρεῖται κακίας.
thought_title: The old examples as a type for warning the Corinthians
orientation: Gennadius is opening his comment on 1 Corinthians 10:15, explaining why Paul sets the ancient Israelites before the Corinthians as a warning example.
pass_a_gloss: In these things he wishes to instruct them in what is fitting from the setting-beside of the ancients, showing that those also experienced events that served as types. For thus, since the example appeared suitable, he was found justly advising them not to commit similar offenses, in order that they might not suffer similar things. Now their being under the cloud was a clear sign of the grace of the Spirit. For the cloud overshadowing those delivered them from the harm from the Egyptians, and the grace rescues us from demonic evil.

choices.term: ἀπὸ τῆς τῶν παλαιῶν αὐτοὺς παραθέσεως
choices.english: from the setting-beside of the ancients
choices.why: Keeps the literal force of παραθέσεως as placing the ancients alongside the Corinthians for comparison, not a loose 'example'.
rejected: from the example of the ancients
by comparing them with the ancients

choices.why: Uses the fixed glossary rendering 'type' for τύπος, preserving the technical sense of prefiguration.

choices.term: δήλωσις ἦν τῆς τοῦ πνεύματος χάριτος
choices.english: was a clear sign of the grace of the Spirit
choices.why: Renders δήλωσις as 'clear sign' to convey that the cloud visibly indicated the Spirit's grace, not merely symbolized it.
rejected: was a manifestation of the grace of the Spirit
was a declaration of the grace of the Spirit

choices.why: Keeps the present tense of ἐξαιρεῖται to show the ongoing deliverance by grace, and renders κακία as 'evil' rather than 'wickedness' for the demonic force.
rejected: delivers us from the wickedness of demons
takes us out of demonic malice

bible_refs.note: The section is a comment on this verse, though the verse itself is not quoted in the fragment.

pass_b_english: In these verses Paul wants to instruct them in what is fitting by setting the ancients beside them, showing that those people too were deemed worthy of the same things as in a type. For since the example appeared so suitable, he was found to be right in advising them not to commit similar offenses, so that they would not suffer similar things. Their being under the cloud, then, was a clear sign of the grace of the Spirit. For just as the cloud overshadowed those people and delivered them from harm by the Egyptians, so grace rescues us from demonic evil.

last_rejected.quote: deemed worthy of the same things as in a type
last_rejected.source_quote: καθάπερ ἔν τινι τύπῳ τῶν ἴσων ἀξιωθέντας
last_rejected.why: Word order distorted: 'τῶν ἴσων ἀξιωθέντας' = 'deemed worthy of equal things', with 'καθάπερ ἔν τινι τύπῳ' = 'as in a type' modifying how they were deemed worthy. English 'as in a type' dangles awkwardly, suggesting the 'same things' were in a type rather than the Israelites being typologically deemed worthy.
last_rejected.fix: showing that those people too were deemed worthy of the same things by way of a type
last_rejected.ruling: English conveys same meaning: those people deemed worthy of equal things, as in a type. Slight awkwardness, not a major error.

last_rejected.why: 'ἐκ τῶν Αἰγυπτίων' = 'from the Egyptians', not 'by the Egyptians'. The cloud delivered them from harm coming from the Egyptians.
last_rejected.fix: delivered them from harm at the hands of the Egyptians
last_rejected.ruling: 'βλάβης ἐκ τῶν Αἰγυπτίων' = harm from/by Egyptians; 'by' is within normal range for expressing source of harm. Not a major error.

problems.quote: those people too were deemed worthy of the same things as in a type
problems.why: Circular and opaque: 'deemed worthy of the same things as in a type' scrambles type/antitype logic
problems.fix: Those people too experienced events that served as types

problems.why: Same entity called 'grace of the Spirit' then 'Spirit of adoption' without signaling equivalence
problems.fix: Note these refer to the same Spirit

edits.old: showing that those people too were deemed worthy of the same things as in a type.
edits.new: showing that those people too experienced events that served as types.

fixed: The grace of the Spirit and Spirit of adoption refer to the same Spirit; no edit needed as the source itself uses both expressions without explicit equivalence.
